turns.narration:
You open your eyes. The meditation session is half over, and Kira's cushion is still empty. Master Skywalker's footsteps are a slow rhythm on the stone — he's making his way toward you, path curved to pass each student in turn. The generator below the temple coughs and resets, and in the pause you hear the jungle: insects, birds, something heavier moving through underbrush.

Your right hand rests on the Mirialan prayer beads at your belt. Three blank beads still waiting for lessons you haven't learned. The praxeum smells like wet stone and the incense Tionne burns in the archive — sandalwood and something sharper, like the resin from a tree that only grows on Yavin's moon.

Luke stops beside you. His shadow falls across your folded legs. He doesn't speak. He's waiting for you to acknowledge what you've both noticed: that Kira has missed meditation for the third time this week.

The other students breathe in and out, eyes closed. None of them have looked up.
choices: Hold your focus. Stay in the meditation posture. Let Luke see that you trust the session — and that you will find Kira afterward on your own terms.
Rise. Meet his gaze. Say quietly: "I'll go check on her." Offer to handle it before it becomes a matter for the Master's attention.
Reach out with the Force. Sense for Kira's presence in the temple — feel where she is, what she's feeling, why she's not here.
Say nothing, but let your hand drift to the beads. Run your thumb across the blank ones. The meditation posture holds you, but your mind is already pulling toward the jungle.

turns.action: Reach out with the Force. Sense for Kira's presence in the temple — feel where she is, what she's feeling, why she's not here.
turns.narration:
Your palm is flat on the cool stone of the meditation floor. You close your eyes and reach for Kira the way you'd reach for a handhold in the dark — fingers open, trusting the shape will meet you.

The Force answers wrong.

It comes hot and tight, a cramped fist where you expected open air. Not Kira's presence. Something in the stone beneath you, coiled and patient. It knows your name. It knows you're looking for someone and it offers you a bargain: I can show you where she is. Just take what I give you.

You let go.

Your hand lifts off the stone. The presence withdraws, sullen, and the meditation chamber returns to simple light and breath and smelled dust. The other students still breathe in their slow rhythm. Master Skywalker sits at the head of the room, eyes closed, and gives no sign he noticed anything.

You are no closer to finding Kira than when you sat down.

Your shoulder aches from holding the sitting position too long. The wrong temperature of that dark presence lingers at the edge of your awareness, not quite gone, like a note that hasn't finished vibrating. You open your eyes. The afternoon light slants through the temple openings, and Kira's cushion is still empty.
choices: Wait until meditation ends. Follow Luke out. Tell him Kira missed again — let him decide whether to act on it.
Don't interrupt the session. Stand up anyway. Go find Kira the old way — look where she might be, ask the people who saw her last.
Sit still. Stay the whole session. But keep your hand on the stone — let that presence know you're not afraid of it, even if you won't use it.

turns.action: Don't interrupt the session. Stand up anyway. Go find Kira the old way — look where she might be, ask the people who saw her last.
turns.narration:
You rise from the meditation cushion in one motion — no hesitation, no bow to the session. Master Skywalker's eyes open, track you, offer nothing but a slight nod. The other students breathe on. Their stillness makes your movement feel like noise.

The hall outside is empty. You check Kira's quarters first — door open, bed made, a half-finished holonovel facedown on her desk. Not there. The training dojo: empty. The library: Tionne looks up from a datapad, tilts her head.

"I'm looking for Kira."

Tionne sets the datapad down. "She came through here about an hour ago. Said she wanted to check something in the lower levels. I told her those sections aren't cleared yet — the structural scans show instability near the old refectory. She said she'd be careful."

A pause. Tionne's fingers rest on the datapad screen, not moving.

"She's been going down there a lot this week," she says. Not a question. An observation left for you to fill.

You don't fill it.

The stairwell to the lower Massassi levels is behind a blast door that someone jury-rigged a proximity lock onto. The lock is disengaged. The door stands open. The air that comes up is cooler than the temple air, and it carries a smell of wet stone and something older — mineral, metallic, like the inside of a cave where nothing has breathed in centuries.
choices: Step through the door. If Kira's down there, you can find her quickly — and if there's something wrong, you'll know it faster alone than waiting for permission. But you'll go in without telling anyone where you're heading.

Head back to the meditation hall and catch Luke before the session ends. Tell him what Tionne said, what you felt during meditation, and ask him to come with you. It's slower, but you won't face whatever's down there on your own.
Check the cargo bay first — Kira sometimes takes a speeder into the jungle for fresh air. The lower levels could wait until you're sure she didn't just slip out for a ride.
Stand in the open doorway and reach out with the Force again — try to sense her presence from here, not from a meditation mat but from the edge of the dark itself.

turns.action: Head back to the meditation hall and catch Luke before the session ends. Tell him what Tionne said, what you felt during meditation, and ask him to come with you. It's slower, but you won't face whatever's down there on your own.
turns.narration:
You walk back into the meditation hall. The session is still in progress—nine students seated in loose rows, eyes closed, breathing in and out. Master Skywalker is at the front, seated cross-legged, his hands resting on his knees.

He opens his eyes when you enter.

He doesn't stand. Doesn't speak. Just watches you cross the stone floor and kneel a few feet away, close enough to speak without raising your voice above the rhythm of breathing around you.

"Something's wrong," you say. "Kira's been going into the lower levels. Tionne mentioned old Massassi architecture. Dark side history."

Luke's expression doesn't change, but something in his posture shifts—a stillness that wasn't there a moment ago.

"I felt something during meditation," you continue. "Under the temple. Like a presence. Cold. Patient. And Kira isn't here, Master. She wasn't in the jungle. She's down there."

He considers this for three full breaths.

"The lower levels contain a vergence in the Force," he says. "Old. Disturbed by the construction. I've been monitoring it."

"And Kira?"

"She knows the ruins are restricted." He says it flatly. Not defensive. Not dismissive. A fact stated for the record.

You wait.

He looks past you, toward the open archway where the afternoon light falls across the stone. "I trusted her to follow the rules. Perhaps that was my error. Or perhaps she has a reason she hasn't shared."

His eyes return to yours.

"What do you want to do?"
choices: Go down there together. Right now. Before the session ends. Whatever she's found, you should see it too.
Ask him what he knows about the vergence — what he's found, what he's been waiting for. You need the full picture before you move.
Tell him you'll find her. Alone. This isn't about rules anymore — it's about your friend, and you need him to trust your judgment.

turns.action: Tell him you'll find her. Alone. This isn't about rules anymore — it's about your friend, and you need him to trust your judgment.
turns.narration:
He looks at you for a long moment. Not measuring. Not deciding. Just seeing you — the way a teacher sees a student they've been watching without comment.

"All right."

He says it simply. No elaboration. No conditions. But he doesn't move, and his voice drops half a register.

"Find her. Bring her back — or bring me to where she is. But if you find something you can't handle, you signal. I don't care how embarrassed you'll feel about it later."

A beat. The corner of his mouth moves, just barely.

"I was eighteen when I walked into a Hutt's throne room with a borrowed blaster and no plan. Trusting your judgment, I understand. Trusting it blindly — that's what I'm asking you not to do."

He steps past you, toward the meditation hall, then stops.

"The lower levels — the sealed stairs past the old power station. That's where the vergence is strongest. If she's drawn to it, she'll be there. Take a glow rod. The temple's power grid doesn't reach that deep."

He doesn't look back.

The meditation hall's blast door hisses open, then closed behind him. You're alone in the corridor. The afternoon light has shifted to a deeper gold, and from the stairwell behind you, the cool air still rises — stone and mineral and something else. Something that waits.
choices: Head straight for the sealed stairs. Kira's been gone too long already — every minute of hesitation is a minute you're not with her.
Stop by your quarters first. Grab the glow rod Luke mentioned, a stimpack, maybe the old datapad. Being prepared isn't the same as being afraid.
Go find Tionne in the archives. She knows the history of these ruins — she might know something about what's drawing Kira, something Luke didn't say.
Pause at the stairwell entrance. Reach out with the Force before you descend — sense what's waiting below before you commit to the dark.

turns.action: Go find Tionne in the archives. She knows the history of these ruins — she might know something about what's drawing Kira, something Luke didn't say.
turns.narration:
The archives occupy what was once a Massassi war room. The ceiling is low enough that you have to duck under the central beam—the original builders were shorter than humans, and the stone remembers their proportions. Tionne has hung glow lamps at intervals, casting the room in a warm amber that fights the chill radiating from the walls.

She's at the far table, cross-legged, a datapad in one hand and a physical flimsiplast scroll unrolled across her lap. She doesn't look up when your boots scrape the threshold, but her hand stops moving.

"The lower levels," you say. "Something in them. Kira missed meditation again, and when I reached for her—" You stop. The wrong temperature of that presence is still in your chest, a cold that has nothing to do with the stone.

Tionne sets the datapad down. Her eyes are pale in the lamplight, and they hold yours for a long moment before she speaks.

"The Great Temple was built on an older structure. The Massassi didn't clear the site—they buried it and built over it." She gestures to the scroll. "I found a reference last night. The lower chambers were a meditation space for the original dark side practitioners. Not Sith, exactly. Something older. Something the Sith absorbed."

She taps the scroll. "The vergence you felt—it's not new. It's been sealed for thousands of years. The question is what opened it."

You step closer. The scroll shows architectural diagrams—a cross-section of the temple with a hollow space beneath the foundation, drawn in angular lines that hurt to follow.

"Was Kira down there?"

Tionne's silence is an answer.

"She's been drawn to it," you say. "Luke knows. He didn't tell me."

"He tells you what he thinks you need." Tionne's voice is careful, the voice of someone who has learned to navigate silences. "The question is whether you trust his judgment—or whether you need to see for yourself."

The scroll shows three access points. One leads from the old power station. One from a collapsed tunnel in the eastern wing. One from a well in the jungle, half a kilometer from the temple's outer wall.

The air in the archives smells of old paper and preservative chemicals. One of the glow lamps flickers, fails for a second, and returns.
choices: Follow the scroll's access route through the old power station—it's the closest, and you know the way from earlier today. Efficiency matters more than caution.
Take the jungle well route. It's farther, but it approaches from outside the temple entirely—less chance of being seen if someone is watching the main entrances.
Sit down across from Tionne and ask her the question you haven't asked yourself: why you need to find Kira alone, when Luke offered to help you.
